- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 2-period moving average to smooth.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias correction proportional to deviation from 75–80 range.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted average of 7–14 day window to dampen volatility.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0–0.2 values (e.g., 3+ consecutive), model underperforms; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast.
- When true outcome is below 70, model often misses the drop; apply lag correction: if 3+ prior days <70, forecast should be ≤70 unless sentiment >0.6.
